newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL plunges, pulls BUX down from peak.
newsitem.headline: MOL plunges, pulls BUX down from peak.

text.p: The last stronghold of the Budapest Stock Exchange fell on Wednesday as shares in oil company MOL, surging in the past few days, moved sharply lower on profit-taking, traders said.
The BUX index fell 131.10 points to end at 5,368.64.
The index's plunge did not catch traders unguarded as the Hungarian share market has rocketed around 30 percent since the beginning of the year, thus a correction was expected.
"This correction was in the air, I was not surprised," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities. "MOL's fall also could be expected."
MOL shares opened sharply lower, at 3,350 forints, below Tuesday's close of 3,425 forints and slid to as low as 3,080 forints before recovering to close at 3,180, down 245.
"MOL...took the BUX index on its shoulders in the past two days so one could expect the trend to reverse sooner or later," one trader said earlier today. "We can call this profit-taking."

Earlier this week MOL bucked the market's declining trend and its strong gains -- from Friday's close of 3,080 forints to a new record high of 3,480 on Tuesday -- pushed the BUX index to new highs while most other key stocks drifted lower.
On Wednesday almost all leading stocks, including all chemicals, pharmaceuticals and bank shares fell.
Chemicals company TVK fell seven percent or 175 forints to close at 2,350 forints, while Borsodchem lost 3.6 percent to end at 5,750.
Hotelier Danubius also drifted lower but only after reaching a new record high of 5,335 forints. It finished at 5,150, down 130.
Traders said they expected the market's downward trend to continue this week, ahead of the release of companies' preliminary annual results by the February 15 deadline.
"I think prices will drop in the short-term and annual results could give prices new guidance," Forgo said.
"Annual results will justify in certain cases the recent high prices so I expect many stocks to rebound," he added.
